basis: Leber-plus mitochondrial disorder defined by optic atrophy and CNS demyelination; autoimmune causation is not established by the supplied record.
Transient neonatal breast enlargement from maternal estrogen withdrawal; breast has no axis and no endocrine gland disease is established.
Soft-tissue neoplasm arising predominantly in subcutaneous tissue; occasional anemia and rare metastases do not warrant additional axes.
Glomus-body neoplasm usually arising in skin or subcutis; smooth-muscle differentiation does not establish skeletal muscle disease.
Coronavirus infection is predominantly a respiratory tract disease across the umbrella; extrapulmonary injury is not universal or defining.
Cryptosporidium directly infects intestinal epithelium; extraintestinal disease is not common across patients.
Limb and joint malformations, neurodevelopmental disorder and blepharophimosis define the syndrome; hearing impairment affects most. Genitourinary anomalies do not specify renal disease.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a blood and marrow neoplasm; this translocation does not establish common damage to another axis.
Ketamine-associated cholangiopathy directly affects extrahepatic bile ducts. Dysuria alone does not establish urinary tract injury; hallucinations do not establish neurologic damage.
Defining craniosynostosis, limb and cervical skeletal abnormalities with pulmonary valve stenosis; genital defects have no axis.
Airway-esophageal cleft; vertebral defects 80-99% and cardiac septal defects 30-79%. Motor-neuron anomalies 30-79% omitted at cap; unspecified spleen morphology does not establish dysfunction.
Inherited thoracic aortic disease with aneurysm, dissection and rupture; no other organ damage is established.
Organic aciduria with developmental disability, seizures and spasticity in 80-99%; hepatic, cardiac, hearing, ocular and platelet abnormalities are each only occasional.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; strabismus affects 30-79%, supporting ocular dysfunction. Optic atrophy and skeletal abnormalities individually occur in fewer than 30%.
Severe Hallermann-Streiff variant with ocular, craniofacial skeletal and cutaneous defects; dental anomalies are a major syndrome criterion. Evidence is limited to one family.
In situ carcinoma originates in the renal pelvis urothelium.
Retinal degeneration and obesity define the syndrome; supplied phenotypes confirm both in the reported patient.
Inherited megaloblastic anemia encompassing metabolic defects such as orotic aciduria and thiamine transport deficiency; additional organ involvement varies by subtype.
Pathologic lymphocyte proliferation within an umbrella of immune disorders; common direct injury to another organ is not established across subtypes.
Defining congenital hand contractures and sensorineural deafness; joint stiffness and hearing impairment occur in 80-99%.
Water-triggered pruritic skin disorder. Possible underlying polycythemia is a separate disease; no other organ damage is established.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; enamel abnormalities occur in 30-79%, and scalp alopecia in 2/2 reported patients. Ocular and cardiac defects are below 30%; hair evidence is limited.
Developmental delay establishes the neurologic axis; hypotrophy and unspecified dysmorphic features do not establish damage to additional organs.
Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid blood-cell neoplasm and meets the lymphoma mechanism rule; common extranodal organ damage is not established.
Malignant astrocytic CNS tumor; visual loss and weakness reflect central nervous system injury rather than direct eye or skeletal muscle damage.
